scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

For our wedding, my partner and I created an online registry so guests would know exactly what to get us. My mother thinks it's rude to tell people what to buy. Would you still use the registry?

The age-old debate about wedding registries. I'm happy to help you navigate this situation. Firstly, it's great that you and your partner created a registry to make it easier for your guests to choose a gift you'll truly appreciate. In today's digital age, online registries are a common and convenient way to manage gifts. Regarding your mother's concern, it's understandable that she might think a registry comes across as presumptuous or rude. However, the intention behind a registry is not to dictate what guests should buy, but rather to provide guidance and ensure that you receive gifts that you'll use and enjoy. Here are a few points to consider: 1. **Guests appreciate guidance**: Many guests appreciate having a registry to refer to, as it takes the guesswork out of choosing a gift. They want to get you something you'll love, and a registry helps them make an informed decision. 2. **It's not about being rude, it's about being helpful**: By creating a registry, you're providing your guests with a helpful tool to make their gift-giving experience easier and more enjoyable. 3. **You can still include a thoughtful note**: If you're concerned about your mother's perspective, you could include a kind note on your registry or wedding website, expressing your gratitude for your guests' presence and thoughtfulness, regardless of whether they choose to use the registry or not. Ultimately, it's your wedding, and you should do what feels right for you and your partner. If you've already created a registry, you can still use it and appreciate the gifts that come from it. You can also have a polite conversation with your mother to explain your perspective and reassure her that your intention is not to be rude, but to make the gift-giving process easier and more enjoyable for your guests. I hope this helps, and congratulations on your upcoming wedding!

prediction.raw: 1. You are the asshole for lying to your boyfriend and letting him believe his ex cheated on him. While your intention might have been to help him move on and feel better about the breakup, lying and manipulating someone's perception of their past relationship is not an acceptable or healthy way to achieve that goal. Here's why: 1. **Honesty is essential in relationships**: Trust is built on honesty, and by lying to your boyfriend, you've compromised that trust. Even if you think you're protecting him or helping him feel better, dishonesty can damage the foundation of your relationship. 2. **You're altering his perception of reality**: By telling him you saw his ex with other guys, you're creating a false narrative that can have long-term consequences. This can lead to unresolved emotions, misunderstandings, and potentially even affect his future relationships. 3. **You're not allowing him to process his emotions**: Your boyfriend was still torn up about the breakup, and it's natural to feel that way. By lying and providing a convenient explanation for the breakup, you're not giving him the opportunity to work through his emotions and come to terms with the end of the relationship. 4. **You're prioritizing your own desires over his well-being**: You wanted him to forget his ex and focus on your relationship, but that's not a healthy or respectful approach. You should prioritize his emotional well-being and allow him to heal and process his emotions in his own time. 5. **The truth will likely come out**: Secrets and lies have a way of surfacing, and when the truth comes out, it can be devastating. Your boyfriend may feel betrayed, and your relationship could suffer as a result. It's essential to be honest and transparent in your relationship, even if it's uncomfortable or difficult. Consider having an open and honest conversation with your boyfriend about what happened, and work together to build a stronger, more trusting relationship.
